title: Your long discourse
hookLine: of the long discourses, which one stays with you
last: WHAT HELPS, WHAT TO LET GO.

lines: WHICH ROOM DO YOU LIVE IN?
cards: Ask ten people who read the same novel what they remember, and you'll get ten different scenes. One remembers the storm. One, a line at a kitchen table.
One, a side character nobody else noticed. Nine of them didn't read it wrong. A long book is a house with many rooms, and each reader ends up living in one.
For seven weeks, this path has walked through the thirty-four Long Discourses. Kings, gods, wanderers, a courtesan, a skeptic prince, a young man bowing to the sky. Today adds nothing new.

teach.h: A MOONLIT KING, A STAIRCASE, A MEAL
teach.b: Some scenes, in case one is waiting for you. A king who killed his own father rides out under a full moon, asking what a spiritual life is good for, and hears that even a slave who goes forth would be honored by a king.
A man builds a staircase to a palace he has never seen. A woman named Ambapali invites the Buddha to a meal, and when princes ask for the same day, he keeps his word to her.
The Buddha, old and ill, tells Ananda there's no teacher's closed fist: nothing held back. Ananda weeps by a door, and the Buddha praises his long kindness as an attendant.
A skeptical prince argues with a monk through story after story.
And this week: young Sigala, bowing to six directions, learns what each bow could mean. Six ways wealth leaks away. How to tell a true friend.
Duties that run both ways, between parents and children, teachers and students, spouses, friends, workers. Then Sariputta, counting so nothing is lost, and counting again by tens.

teach.h: THE TEACHING WILL BE YOUR TEACHER
teach.b: In the last journey, the Buddha says that after he's gone, the teaching and the discipline will be the teacher. Not a person, not a successor: the words. And words do their work by being remembered.

teach.h: THE SCENE THAT STAYED IS YOURS
teach.b: So the scene that stays with you isn't trivia.
It's the teacher you actually took home, and it doesn't have to match anyone else's.

how: Individual long discourses, such as the account of the Buddha's last days or the advice to Sigala, are read, chanted and taught on their own in Buddhist communities.

games.q: the Buddha is dying. the monks wonder who will lead them. what does he leave as their teacher?
games.why: in the last journey he says the teaching and discipline he gave will be their teacher after he is gone.

practice: Let one scene from these weeks come up on its own, whichever arrives first, and walk into it slowly: where is it, what time of day, who is speaking, what does the air feel like?
Stay inside it for a few breaths, the way you'd stand in a room you love. Then notice why this one came, without explaining it, and rest.

wordCard.voice: Digha Nikaya, the long collection: the one scene, out of thirty-four discourses, that stayed with you, the teaching you actually carried home. Today's word.
